text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A 1985 edict denies Kuwaiti women the right to vote in parliamentary elections or to run for a parliament seat in contradiction with the country's constitution. Kuwait women, slighty more than half of Kuwait's 700,000 citizens, have been campaigning for political rights.
- Minister of Communications Jassem al-Oun says his ministry collected revenues of 85 million dinars ($284 million) in 1996.

- Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) to privatise Livestock Transport and Trading Company, the Public Warehousing Company and Kuwait Public Transport Company. A report by the state's accounting bureau has recommended the privatisation of part of the national flag carrier Kuwait Airways Corp.
- Riot and unrest at Central Prison. Security sources said the unrest was launched by prisoners awaiting execution for illicit drug offenses.

- Information Ministry sets teams to monitor music shows and dance parties. Violators will be dealt with severely. Several Islamist parliamentarians have been demanding a ban on all concerts in conservative Kuwait.
- MPs demand debate on rising crime wave.
